The fantasy point projection (F1) serves as a forward-looking signal, while past performance (F2-F4) provides backward validation. These are normalized through a scaling coefficient (A), which varies by sport and role, reflecting differential impact. The global salary floor (GSF) introduces an economic constraint that limits the feasible set of players. This creates a dual optimization problem: maximizing projected value subject to GSF constraints. The system exhibits duality between predictive modeling and resource allocation, where failure modes include overfitting to recent data or ignoring economic realities. Temporal coherence is maintained via exponentially decaying weights for recent performance, ensuring relevance without bias.
